findings.reason: the section's entire write path is the gate-log helper, so implemented as written it relaxes nothing and its own done-when cannot pass.
findings.text: §2 names the reader as being in `reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py` near lines 1021–1092 and takes that file as its write path, but that region is the gate-log check (`_log_shows_the_command_ran` at promotion_evidence.py:1017, `_recorded_exit_status` at promotion_evidence.py:1044); the reader that refuses a control log with no `EXIT=` is `_require_declared_negative_control` at promotion_checks.py:2029 (refusal at promotion_checks.py:2159), and it has a second write-time twin, `_control_log_findings` at reports.py:2031 (refusal "records no exit status" at reports.py:2101), which the section never names — a worker writing a runner-only control log is therefore still refused by `crew check --manifest` after the planned edit and the halt moves earlier rather than away

findings.reason: the section must name the one parser it changes and reconcile the other call sites, or the same halt reappears through a path the plan did not touch.
findings.text: a census of the terminal-`EXIT=` parser: two independent implementations of one reading exist, `reports.py:1293 _terminal_exit_status` and `promotion_checks.py`'s imported copy `promotion_evidence.py:1044 _recorded_exit_status`, and the first is consulted by a second refusal at reports.py:1495 as well as the control check at reports.py:2098 — §2 relaxes one owner without naming the census, so "is a terminal EXIT required" gets three different answers

findings.reason: putting the floor in `lane_context` places a policy decision inside a classifier and leaves the assignment path untouched, so the 8-minute node keeps its 8 minutes and the section's reproduction would not be repaired.
findings.text: §5 names `reckon/crew/picker/lane_context.py` (its lines 173 and 388) as where the budget is assigned, but `lane_context._size_of` (lane_context.py:163) only classifies a budget the node already declares, for profile lookup, and it delegates to `run_time_profile._size_class` (run_time_profile.py:179), documented there as the one owner of the budget-versus-token thresholds; the budget a brief-based node actually receives is assigned at dispatch_plan.py:796-800 (`default_budget = resolved_time_budget(config, backend)`; `node.time_budget = node.time_budget or default_budget)`, with the fence it must clear read at dispatch_plan.py:885 (`resolved_time_ceiling`)

findings.reason: the section reads as a new reader when it is a one-condition relaxation of an existing one, and saying so shrinks the node and prevents a third failure-id parser beside `gate_log_failure_ids`.
findings.text: §2's deliverable asks the reader to admit a log whose "test runner's own output in it shows the run failed and names at least one failing test id the head arm passes", but `_control_failure_ids` (promotion_checks.py:1937) already reads exactly that through `review.gate_log_failure_ids` (review.py:2106, with pytest and ctest arms at review.py:2053 and review.py:2078), and `_head_suite_failure_ids`/`_baseline_suite_failure_ids` (promotion_checks.py:1995/1955) already perform the head-then-baseline comparison; the only new behaviour is dropping the `EXIT=` requirement

findings.reason: the plan adds a third answer to "does this edit need a review" without naming the two that exist, so the three will disagree on the same edit and the coordinator cannot tell which governs.
findings.text: §6 proposes that `--accept-edits` make `review_coverage` treat edited units as covered, but `review_coverage` already carries that rule: an answered-as-`acted` finding covers the edit that followed it (`_acted_finding_units`, called at plan_review.py:1291, defined around plan_review.py:2687), and `review_need.judge` (review_need.py:167) already decides whether a change needs a new review at all — neither is cited in §6

findings.reason: a second cover channel inside one function is exactly the surface this item refuses; the section must extend the acted-finding owner or say what it cannot express.
findings.text: §6 layers an acceptance record as a parallel cover path beside `--acted` dispositions, and states no reason why `_acted_finding_units` cannot be extended (for example by recording the coordinator's reason and session on the disposition it already stores)

findings.reason: the section must account for the added option and the added refusal family in its own text, as the item requires.
findings.text: §3 adds `crew dispatch --over-fence REASON` and a new refusal wording in `node.py:1362`, against cli_options 465 and refusal_families 23, with no statement of what it retires or merges

findings.reason: the option and how it shares validation with `queue edit` is the section's substance and belongs in its text.
findings.text: §4 adds `crew resume --time-budget`, confirmed absent from `crew_resume` (crew_run_commands.py:2175-2189), and the `--over-fence` companion rule, with no accounting; the nearest existing surface is `crew queue edit --time-budget` (crew_run_commands.py:2429), and the section does not say why resume cannot share its parsing and fence check

findings.reason: the section must place the option relative to the existing answer dispositions (`RESPONSE_ACTIONS`, plan_review.py:282) rather than add a fourth way to say "answered".
findings.text: §6 adds `crew review --plan --accept-edits "REASON"`, a new CLI option and a new stored record shape, against cli_options 465, with no statement of what it retires or merges

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — every section adds one predicate to a module that already owns that decision (`review_coverage`, `node.validate_node`, `_require_declared_negative_control)`, so no new module's interface exceeds the behaviour it hides.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2 names the wrong owner (`promotion_evidence.py`, which holds the gate-log reader) and §5 names a classifier that owns no budget assignment; the real owners are `promotion_checks.py:2029` with `reports.py:2031`, and `dispatch_plan.py:796`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 2362, cli_options 465, mcp_views 15, refusal_families 23; §3, §4 and §6 each add a CLI option (`--over-fence`, `--time-budget` on resume, `--accept-edits`) and none names what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §6 adds `--accept-edits` as a new coverage channel while `_acted_finding_units` and `review_need.judge` already own "the edit that answers a finding is covered", and §2 proposes to teach a reader to read a runner's `FAILED` ids when `_control_failure_ids` already does exactly that.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §6's acceptance record is a second cover path laid beside `_acted_finding_units` with no statement of why that owner cannot be extended.
